pairs.difference: A (hat): key light from upper left. The crown's right side and the underside of the brim fall into a clear shadow side, and the brim casts a dark shadow onto the crown. B (scout jacket): lit flat from the front. The sleeves and the chest get almost the same light on both sides, and the shadow under the collar and cuffs is shallow and warm-tinted. The lens shows an even golden glow with no clear light side.
pairs.fix: Light the jacket from the upper left. Put the right sleeve and right side of the body in a clearly darker shadow, add a dark shadow under the collar and inside the cuffs, and keep the shadows cool, not golden.

pairs.difference: A (rope): side light from the left. The coils have a rounded light-to-dark turn and the rope casts a long, dark shadow to the right on the sand. B (mower): light from the upper right. The red hood has a broad soft sheen, the left side and wheels sit in shadow, and the grass has a short contact shadow. Both have one clear light direction and real-range depth, so lighting gives no reason to pick either.

A (umbrella): strong light from above. The canopy top is bright and the underside panels drop into a deep, dark shadow, so the form turns clearly. B (sheriff star): lit straight from the front and evenly. All five points have the same soft pillowy shading with no side darker than the others, the ring has no shadow side, and the light-side bias is nearly zero (0.115). Form contrast is 0.303, below the real range.
pairs.fix: Light the star badge from the upper left. Make the lower-right points and the lower-right arc of the ring noticeably darker, give each point a sharp ridge with one lit face and one shadowed face, and drop a soft shadow down and to the right behind the badge.

pairs.difference: A (cactus): lit from the front. The trunk and arms are shaded almost the same on both sides, and the ribs only show soft, shallow banding. Form contrast is 0.367, below the real range. B (spring duck): strong key light from the upper left. The duck's right side and belly go into deep shadow, and a long, dark shadow falls to the left on the sand from the spring base.
pairs.fix: Light the cactus from the upper left. Make its right side and the undersides of the arms clearly darker, give each rib a lit edge and a shadowed groove, and add a firm contact shadow where the trunk meets the sand.

pairs.difference: A (ice tray): light from the upper front left. The tray's front faces are lit, its sides darker, and there is a cast shadow on the wooden table. B (fruit plate): seen from above under flat, even light. The fruit has little shadow side, and the plate only has a faint, soft shadow ring. The light-side bias is low (0.293).
pairs.fix: Light the fruit plate from the upper left. Put dark shadow sides on the right of the orange slices, grapes and berries, and cast a clear shadow from the fruit onto the plate and from the plate onto the table to the lower right.

pairs.difference: A (sneakers): lit softly like a studio photo. The shoes have a rounded realistic sheen and a large, soft cast shadow to the left, but the measured light-side bias is close to zero (0.019) and the shading range is above the real range. B (horseshoe): light from the left. The metal turns smoothly into shadow on the right arm, with a clean cast shadow on the wood behind it.
pairs.fix: Light the sneakers from one strong upper-side light. Put a clearly darker shadow side on the far side of each shoe and make the cast shadow short and firm under the soles, not a wide studio haze.

pairs.difference: A (campfire tripod): the fire is a visible light source, yet the pot and logs get no warm firelight from below. The poles and stones are lit evenly from the front. The shading range (0.58) and light-side bias (0.178) are both below the real range. B (gas pump): sunset light from the right. It puts a warm rim on the pump's right edge, the left face sits in shadow, and the base casts a shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the pot's underside, the inner faces of the logs and the bottoms of the poles with warm orange glow from the fire. Keep the outer sides of the stones and poles in darker shadow, away from the fire.

pairs.difference: A (saloon): flat front sunlight. The facade, the porch posts and the side wall are nearly the same brightness, and the shadow under the porch roof is shallow. B (dock): light from the upper left. The posts drop into dark shadow sides, the life ring has a clear lit top and shaded bottom, and the posts cast shadows on the water.
pairs.fix: Light the saloon from the upper left. Put the right side wall in clear shadow, add a deep shadow under the porch roof across the doors and windows, and cast the building's shadow onto the ground to the right.

pairs.difference: A (rowboat): light from the upper left at a moderate strength. The hull's inner wall and outer side turn smoothly into shadow, and there is soft contact shading at the dock. B (wagon): lit by a painted sun. The canvas cover and wheels have hazy, muddy shading. Light-side bias (0.851) and form contrast (0.659) are both above the real range, so the shading is pushed rather than modeled the way the real cards do it.
pairs.fix: Light the wagon with clean light from the upper left. Give the canvas cover a smooth roll from a bright top to a medium shadow underneath, give the wheels crisp lit rims, and put a firm shadow under the wagon bed.

pairs.difference: A (saddle): lit evenly from the front like an app icon. The left and right flaps are the same brightness and the saddle casts no shadow on the wooden beam. Light-side bias is 0.149, below the real range. B (fountain): light from the left. The basins' right sides turn darker, the tiers cast shadows on the pool below, and the base has contact darkening on the tiles.
pairs.fix: Light the saddle from the upper left. Make the right flap and the underside of the seat clearly darker, cast the saddle's shadow onto the wooden beam, and put a dark shadow under the stirrup straps.

pairs.difference: A (cowboy boots): flat frontal light. Both boots are lit almost the same on every side with only soft, shallow modeling. Light-side bias is 0.069, below the real range. B (flip-flops): light from the upper left. The straps cast small shadows on the soles, and the sole edges have a darker side to the lower right.
pairs.fix: Light the boots from the upper left. Put the right side of each boot shaft and the heel in noticeably darker shadow, and add a shadow where the front boot overlaps the back one.

pairs.difference: A (guitar on stage): two spotlights are drawn, but the guitar body is lit evenly from the front. There is no warm and cool split from the two lamps, and only a soft contact shadow on the floor. B (caravan): light from the left. The caravan's right side and rear go into a deep blue shadow, the wheel arch has a dark core, and the grass gets a cast shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the guitar from the two stage spotlights. Give the left edge of the body a warm yellow highlight and the right edge a cool blue rim, keep the middle of the body darker, and cast two crossing shadows onto the stage floor.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away with flat, frontal, nearly even light. Both sides of the object are lit the same, the shadow side stays shallow and tinted warm, and cast and contact shadows are soft, weak or missing. Visible light sources (fires, spotlights, a painted sun) don't actually light the object. Real cards commit to one key light from the upper side, with a clearly darker shadow side and a firm shadow cast onto the surface.
